{"explanation": "Baseline feedback shows a successful fit (mse ~0.0313, nmse ~0.1907) with 8 declared parameters. The only observed evidence is a working but restricted feature set: one bilinear term (u0*u1) and no quadratic or other cross terms, so any curvature in u0*u2, u1*u2, or pure quadratics is left unexplained and acts as structured residual. I therefore keep the exact same signature, input order, parameter-index linear structure (bounded least squares from ones), and scaling envelope, and add six strictly linear-in-parameter basis terms (c8..c13) spanning the missing pair products and self-quadratics inside the same scaled envelope. This preserves the well-conditioned 'core * (1+c1 u0)(1+c2 u1)(1+c2 u2)' form that already fits, while enlarging the span so the residual curvature can be absorbed, raising the declared count from 8 to 14. Output remains a finite float64 array of shape (len(u0),) via nan_to_num, with no I/O, files, or extra packages. Indices are guarded so any n_params from 0..16 yields valid behavior. Trade-off accepted: 6 more parameters for a larger linear-in-params span; if the added terms are not needed the bounded least-squares fit simply drives their weights toward zero.", "n_params": 14, "security_risk": "LOW", "source": "import numpy as np


def equation(u0, u1, u2, params):
    """Expanded polynomial-in-scaled-input response; strictly linear in params."""
    u0 = np.asarray(u0, dtype=float)
    u1 = np.asarray(u1, dtype=float)
    u2 = np.asarray(u2, dtype=float)

    c = np.asarray(params, dtype=float).ravel()
    n = c.size

    c0 = c[0] if n > 0 else 0.0
    c1 = c[1] if n > 1 else 0.0
    c2 = c[2] if n > 2 else 0.0
    c3 = c[3] if n > 3 else 0.0
    c4 = c[4] if n > 4 else 0.0
    c5 = c[5] if n > 5 else 0.0
    c6 = c[6] if n > 6 else 0.0
    c7 = c[7] if n > 7 else 0.0
    c8 = c[8] if n > 8 else 0.0
    c9 = c[9] if n > 9 else 0.0
    c10 = c[10] if n > 10 else 0.0
    c11 = c[11] if n > 11 else 0.0
    c12 = c[12] if n > 12 else 0.0
    c13 = c[13] if n > 13 else 0.0

    s0 = 1.0 + c1 * u0
    s1 = 1.0 + c2 * u1
    s2 = 1.0 + c3 * u2

    core = (c0
            + c4 * u0
            + c5 * u1
            + c6 * u2
            + c7 * u0 * u1
            + c8 * u0 * u2
            + c9 * u1 * u2
            + c10 * u0 * u0
            + c11 * u1 * u1
            + c12 * u2 * u2
            + c13 * u0 * u1 * u2)

    out = core * s0 * s1 * s2

    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)", "summary": "Extend baseline with quadratic and pair-bilinear terms, 14 parameters"}
